title: A service that compiles user-supplied regexps into native executable patterns trusts the compiler's own arithmetic
index_line: T-0068 · MEM_WRITE · CI-config regexps compile to native pcode; the repeat-count program-size arithmetic overflows the allocation and crafted bytecode takes over · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: The application treated Regexp.new as a safe pure function. Down in the engine, compilation is native memory work driven by attacker-sized arithmetic — and an integer overflow in the compiled-pattern's program size let user input allocate far too little and write far too much.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated CI lint request (or a committed CI configuration) carries a crafted regexp with a huge bounded repeat of a compile-heavy subexpression
the engine compiles the pattern into native bytecode; the repeat-expansion program-size arithmetic overflows (signed multiplication on the repeat count)
the overflowed size under-allocates the compiled program and the compiler's writes run past it, corrupting engine memory with attacker-shaped bytecode
crafted bytecode stages take over: the public exploit repeats a 37,151-byte lookbehind 57,805 times and drives execution into a system() gadget reached from the engine's crash reporter

source.http.body.value: the CI lint / CI configuration regexp — the lint surface needs no valid user (CVSS 10.0 AV:N/PR:N)

guard.none.value: insufficient regular expression validation: no pre-compilation bound on pattern size or repeat expansion

sink.memory.copy.value: the engine's compiled-program allocation and fill, sized by overflowed arithmetic

size.length.value: the repeat count times per-unit program size — attacker-chosen operands to the overflowing multiplication

preconditions.expr: the target ships an unpatched engine (GitLab CE/EE 19.2<19.2.8, 19.3<19.3.5, 19.4<19.4.2 on Ruby without the program-size patch)
the compile path still overflows on bounded-repeat patterns (patched engines check the expansion with division and reject oversized programs)

check.spec: ruby -e 'begin; Regexp.new("(a?){60000}"); puts "compiled"; rescue => e; puts e.class; end' 2>&1 | head -2

preconditions.expr: the attacker can submit a pattern to any compile surface (lint API, CI config push)

success: the native worker crashes on the crafted pattern (the vendor ships detection for 'Onigmo native worker crash')
controlled execution: the published module drives crafted bytecode into a system() call and opens a session as the GitLab service user
failure_like: patched engine (Ruby 4.0.8 / 3.4.12 / 3.3.13, or GitLab 19.2.8/19.3.5/19.4.2) bounds the repeat expansion and rejects the oversized program
false_positive: ReDoS — slow matching — is match-time complexity, not this record; the overflow here is at compile time
a worker crash alone is a lead: the signature is a program size far beyond the allocation, not mere instability

hazards: every 'compile user regexps' feature — CI config validators, log filters, search-as-regex, rule editors — the engine is native memory work regardless of the host language
the same engine audit produced sibling CVEs: parse-failure double-free after alternation (CVE-2026-89078) and a second integer overflow (CVE-2026-93577 / CVE-2026-110264) — the class, not one bug
exploitation is layout-specific: bytecode offsets move per build; the public module fingerprints the exact release before selecting a native layout
the engine vendor released fixes for all embedders — patch the engine, not only the application
non_transfers: regexp engines that compile to bounded, checked IR and verify program size
deployments that never compile user-supplied patterns

evidence.target: GitLab CE/EE CI/CD regexp compiler on Ruby/Onigmo (CVE-2026-97229, CVSS 3.1 10.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C)

provenance.author: Ruby project (k0kubun)
provenance.corroborates: root cause from the engine vendor: specially crafted patterns corrupt memory while Ruby compiles them; integer overflow in the size of a compiled pattern behind CVE-2026-93577/97229; fixes in Ruby 4.0.8 / 3.4.12 / 3.3.13 with the program-size check applied via division

provenance.author: Rapid7 (metasploit module documentation)
provenance.corroborates: exploit mechanics: lookbehind compiles to 37,151 bytes, repeated 57,805 times, crafted bytecode entered at offset 16,866,665; OP_STEP_BACK_START stages reach a system() gadget; unauthenticated CI lint trigger; per-version native pcode layouts

provenance.author: GitLab (vendor patch release)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-97229: unauthenticated arbitrary code execution via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration; CVSS 10.0; affected versions; Ruby regexp program-size patch shipped in the release
